properties.description:
Layer 2 of the cross-design view (dec:how-a-session-opens-a-view-over-several-designs, option a). crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service/view.rs. The host passes _meta["reflow2/view_graph_ids"] (the hub's members ∩ the caller's readable set) on calls to a hub's own design; call_tool reads it into a task-local (VIEW_GRAPH_IDS) and, when a registry serves the call and the caller rule is a trusted gateway or bearer (the same admission as other_design), view::serve handles it. ROUTED: any string argument ":" makes it a member call — RegistryHandle::member(id) opens the member through service_for (its in-flight guard held so it cannot close under the call) and returns OpenDesign.base.share(), a fresh session for this call (base holds only what the HTTP closure held; no cycle); the prefix is stripped, the view key removed, the caller's writes_for/acting_agent/readable set and verified token carried, so the member's own precheck, write unit and crediting run there and the write is the caller's (AUTHORED_BY read back on the member); node ids in the reply are prefixed back. Two members named in one call: refused ("a write lands in one design; a relation across designs is a typed link record made in one of them"). A member outside the readable set: refused with other_design's sentence (not_readable(), now shared). FAN-OUT: a read-only tool naming no member runs on the hub, then each member in turn, each call awaited to completion before the next — no call ever holds two designs' guards, never the hub's while a member's — and replies {view, by_design, unreachable} with a text block saying it is a view. search_design merges every design's hits ranked by score (each design's own BM25, said in a view_note as not strictly comparable), ids prefixed, stale prefixed. A writer naming no member writes the hub's own design. NOT_VIEWED (hub only, with a view_note): export/import, release/cut and changelog_view, claims, seats, served-text tools (get_instructions, get_skill, list_skills, find_tools, find_skills, describe_schema), and the cross-design tools that already name their other design (compare_designs, compose_and_analyse, describe_designs, pair_designs, seam_report, fork_point, merge_designs, apply_merge, certify_preservation, analyze_alternatives, send_to_design, receive_from_design). PREFIX RULE: values under id/node_id/from_id/to_id/target_id/subject_id/source_id/other_id/artifact_id/decision_id/verification_id/capability_id and any key ending _id; string items under keys ending _ids and in edge sentences; NOT keys ending graph_id/graph_ids, and not

_node_id where the object names its design in

/

_design/

_graph_id (the far end of a cross-design link). No view key: byte-identical to today (proven against a second registry that never admits a view). call_tool's body moved verbatim to call_tool_unshaped; the per-client content shaping is applied once by the dispatcher (the content-policy suites green). HOST CONTRACT ON A WRITE: reflow2 routes a write naming ":" into that member when the member is in the view and readable; it knows no roles, exactly as on a member's own address, where the gateway refuses a view-only caller's write before forwarding. So the host must send, on a write, only the members the caller may change. flo2's gateway does this (feat/the-gateway-hands-reflow2-the-readable-set-and-a-hubs-members, reach.ts viewGraphIds: owner or member on a write, members ∩ readable on a read) and refuses a write naming a view-only member with its usual view-only words; found by the agent that built flo2's half, 2026-10-11. KNOWN LIMITS, recorded: a fan-out reply is bounded per design, not across N; merged search ranks by per-design scores; routing is literal on the 16-hex prefix; the served hub skill does not yet tell agents about prefixed ids. Built 2026-10-11 (169483116, replayed onto main after #721): failing first 7 of 9 (the two that pass before and after are the byte-identical baseline and the deadlock test); after 9 of 9; workspace 3,240 passed, 0 failed; toolsnaps unchanged (197 match). Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.name: A hub's address serves a view over its members when the host names them: a call naming "<graph_id>:<id>" routes to that member, a read naming none fans out per design, search merges, a write lands in the one design it names
